significance.answer:
- Hives at the test site produced significantly more queen brood cells ($p = 0.035$).
- Significantly fewer young queens were found at study locations 400 m distant ($p = 0.021$).
- No adverse effect of clothianidin-treated OSR on bumble bee colony development was observed in terms of hive weight.
- No effect on the number of worker bumble bees was detected.
- At the end of the experiment, the mean number of young queens ranged from 95 (test site distant) to 128 (reference site edge).
- Reproductive success, measured by the sum of young queens and queen brood cells, ranged from 182 (reference site distant) to 216 (reference site edge).
- The sum of queen brood cells and young queens, as an indicator of reproductive success, was not significantly affected by pesticide treatment or the proximity of hives to OSR fields.
